Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the recap — that aligns with our conversation. A few clarifications from our side: 

- High priority: All customer-identifiable PII (account holder names, document uploads, transaction metadata) must remain within the EU and be under our control. That points us toward Private VPC or on-prem for those workloads.
- Non-sensitive workloads (anonymized, aggregated NLP features) could run on Redwood Hosted if the requests are routed to EU-only regions and we have SOC2 evidence + contractual assurances.
- Regions: Primary production presence needs to be Germany (eu-central-1) and Sweden (eu-north-1). Are both available for Private VPC or Dedicated provisioning?
- Cross-region routing: we will need to understand latency and data flow if we split anonymized workloads to hosted endpoints in another EU region. Can Redwood support prefix/KV caching that respects data residency boundaries?
- Timeline: target Q4 2027 rollout for an initial pilot; procurement and security review will need your SOC2 and pen-test summary.

We have attached our security questionnaire (so you can see what we’ll request during vendor review).

Hi Elise / team —

Quick technical note on region availability and routing options: 

- Hosted API: Redwood’s hosted endpoints are available in EU regions (primary: eu-central-1, secondary: eu-west-1). We can guarantee EU-only routing for requests when customers restrict endpoints to those regions. Hosted is quickest to spin up but is multitenant; for PII we recommend Private.
- Dedicated: Reserved GPU pools can be provisioned in eu-central-1. Dedicated provides tenancy isolation and predictable throughput; network isolation is limited compared to Private VPC (we can put it in a customer-specific subnet but traffic still leaves through our managed infra).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): We can deploy a Private control plane and inference nodes inside your VPC in eu-central-1 or on-prem hardware. For Sweden (eu-north-1) we can provision but lead time may be longer (additional capacity request, currently 4–6 weeks).

Cross-region and caching considerations: 
- KV/prefix caching: cache keys and cached content are stored in-region and will not be replicated across EU regions unless explicitly configured. We can enforce region-scoped caches to meet residency requirements.
- Cross-region routing: supported via policy rules (latency/cost/region). We can route anonymized traffic to eu-west-1 hosted endpoints while keeping PII traffic in eu-central-1 private nodes.
- Latency: splitting workloads across eu-central-1 and eu-west-1 typically adds ~10–35ms depending on peering. For strict low-latency SLAs we recommend co-locating Private nodes in the primary region.

Docs and attachments: I’ve attached a short region availability matrix with expected lead times for Dedicated/Private provisioning.

Next steps from infra side: please confirm (1) which specific workloads must be Private in eu-central-1, (2) estimated QPS and token length per workload, and (3) preferred tech-sync slot. We’ll bring a solutions engineer and our security lead if helpful.

Attachments: region-availability-matrix.csv

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
